metadata.notes: Instantiation (b), the plan→implement MODE pair, is the only reading hermes can carry: /plan is a bundled prompt-level skill whose Execution Handoff closes the turn with 'Shall I proceed?' and then executes on approval. The full arc ready→working→waiting→working→ready is derivable from the one shared store — the plan pause IS the turn boundary (2.18's leg), and the approval `user` row resets the waiting cue in messageFold.apply so the ladder falls to transcript_activity for waiting→working. Instantiation (a) (two models, each with its own ModelName) is not available: hermes has no architect/editor pairing, and its aux-model usage lands in session_model_usage, a table this adapter never reads.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: partial
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

Route: record.

## Which instantiation

5.4 admits two instantiations: (a) two MODELS inside one turn (the aider `--architect` shape), and (b) a plan→implement MODE pair across an approval gate, one model throughout — which is how the canonical claudecode sibling is assessed. Hermes is assessed under (b). Everything below is judged against the scenario's own acceptance criteria: the topology `ready → working → waiting → working → ready`, a user-visible waiting episode, final state ready, ≥ 1 tool call, token accumulation across the pair, and a single consistent ModelName.

## (a) is not available on hermes — and would be invisible even if it were

- **No architect/editor pairing exists.** A full-tree case-insensitive grep for `architect` over the installed 0.19.0 source (excluding node_modules and the `architecture`/`architectural` word-family) matches only `plugins/hermes-achievements/dashboard/plugin_api.py` (a "Vibe Architect" achievement) and two creative skill docs. There is no `--architect` flag and no two-model turn loop.
- **The `auxiliary` section is real but is side-task routing, not an editor.** `hermes_cli/config.py` DEFAULT_CONFIG["auxiliary"] carries per-task provider/model slots — `vision`, `web_extract`, `compression`, `skills_hub`, `approval`, `curator`, `kanban_decomposer`, and the post-turn `goal_judge` ("After every turn, a lightweight judge call asks the auxiliary model…"). None of them emits the turn's edits; the main conversation loop does.
- **And the daemon could not see one anyway.** Hermes records aux usage into a SEPARATE table: `record_auxiliary_usage` → `_record_model_usage` writes a per-(model, provider, task) delta into `session_model_usage` "WITHOUT touching the `sessions` summary row" (its own docstring, `hermes_state.py`). Irrlicht's adapter reads only `sessions` and `messages` — `querySessionMetrics` selects `model, cwd, end_reason, started_at, ended_at, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens FROM sessions`, and `foldMessages` replays `messages`. So `ModelName` is `sessions.model`, exactly ONE per session, and `TotalTokens` is that row's `input_tokens + output_tokens`. Live proof, read-only from the maintainer's store (`/Users/ingo/hermes-local/.hermes/state.db`): session `20260726_190232_65c19a` carries THREE `session_model_usage` rows (main loop task='' with 4 API calls, `approval` with 1, `title_generation` with 1) while its `sessions` row exposes a single model and an aggregate that excludes the two aux calls. No session in that store carries more than one distinct model (aux `provider: auto` resolves back to the primary), so the two-ModelName bullet is not merely unobserved — it is not expressible on this transport.

## (b) — hermes does have the mode pair (agent = partial)

- **Architect = the `/plan` phase.** The bundled plan skill (`skills/software-development/plan/SKILL.md`, frontmatter `name: plan` v2.0.0, tags include `plan-mode`) has `# Plan Mode` as its first heading and a Core behavior of "For this turn, you are planning only. Do not implement code." Its deliverable is a markdown plan saved with `write_file` under `.hermes/plans/`. It is exposed as a dynamic slash command (verified live in the 2.18 sibling: `scan_skill_commands()` returns `{'/plan': 'plan'}`), and `/plan <task>` expands into ONE ordinary `user` row — which is why the driver needs no new primitive.
- **The approval gate + editor handoff is prescribed by the skill itself.** Its `## Execution Handoff` section instructs the agent, after saving the plan, to offer: *"Plan complete and saved. Ready to execute using subagent-driven-development — … Shall I proceed?"* and then "When executing, use the `subagent-driven-development` skill". That is literally architect → approval → editor.
- **`partial`, not `yes`, for exactly the 2.18 reason:** the gate is PROMPT-level. 2.18's negative scan over the same installed tree (`plan_mode` / `exit_plan` / "plan mode") found no `exit_plan_mode` tool, no mode enum and no read-only enforcement — only the SKILL.md heading and docs describing OTHER agents. Nothing structurally distinguishes hermes' plan pause from any other trailing-question turn.
- **(b)-specific bonus: the editor phase is ungated by construction.** Hermes' only human approval gate is on the shell tool — `check_all_command_guards` is imported by exactly one module, `tools/terminal_tool.py` (established in the 2.19 sibling); `tools/file_tools.py` `write_file` has no approval call at all. So the implement phase writes a real file with no SECOND permission modal, i.e. no spurious second waiting episode. Hermes gets for free what claudecode's recipe has to buy with `permissions.allow: [Edit, Write]`.

## daemon = full — every leg of the 5-phase arc is derivable today

1. **birth (ready).** Hermes carries a Process matcher, so processlifecycle mints a transient `proc-<PID>` presession at launch; the real `sessions` row is INSERTed on the first user message (~2s later). Hence the birth phase is anchored to `start` UNPINNED and later phases chain off `turn_start`.
2. **ready → working (architect/plan).** The `/plan` expansion lands as a `user` row → `Parser.ParseLine` emits `user_message` → the classifier ladder's total default `transcript_activity` → working.
3. **working → waiting (the plan gate).** The plan turn ends as `role='assistant'` `finish_reason='stop'` whose content carries the ask. `Parser.ParseLine` computes `PendingWaitingCue = ProseIndicatesWaiting(WaitingScanWindow(text))` from the FULL text before truncation and rewrites the SAME row's event type to `turn_done` (`finishReasonEndsTurn`); `classifyAgentDone` consults `IsWaitingForUserInput()` BEFORE routing turn_done → ready, so the session goes working → waiting with no ready in between. This is exactly the leg 2.18 asserts.
4. **waiting → working (the editor/implement recovery) — the leg THIS cell adds.** The approval reply lands as another `user` row. `messageFold.apply` sets `lastEventType = user_message`, empties `openTools` on `ClearToolNames`, and explicitly resets the cue — the adapter carries a dedicated branch for it ("A new user message answers whatever the agent was waiting on, so the cue does not survive it. The ProcessOwnedStore path bypasses the tailer, which is where that reset normally lives"). With `IsAgentDone()` false and `IsWaitingForUserInput()` false, no higher rule in `stateRules` claims the pass (no PermissionPending, no open user-blocking tool, no idle-prompt hold — hermes has no hook tier), so the ladder falls through to `transcript_activity` → waiting → working. No hook and no heuristic is involved.
5. **working → ready.** The implement turn's `finish_reason='stop'` with no trailing cue → `agent_done` → `classifyAgentDone` → ready. `finishReasonEndsTurn` is a denylist, so any terminal reason other than `tool_calls` settles it.

**Tool calls ≥ 1.** Both phases call `write_file`; `decodeToolCalls`/`toolUses` read `messages.tool_calls` (the OpenAI-shaped column) and the matching `role='tool'` row closes the call by `tool_call_id`.

**Cross-phase token accumulation.** Both phases are MAIN-loop API calls, and the CLI path takes the INCREMENT branch of `update_token_counts` (`hermes_state.py`: `input_tokens = input_tokens + ?`; `absolute=True` is documented as the gateway path). So `sessions.input_tokens/output_tokens` grow monotonically across the plan and the implement phase, and the adapter's `TotalTokens = input + output` reads that aggregate. `ModelName` stays a single consistent value (`sessions.model`, `COALESCE`-guarded) — which is what instantiation (b) asks for.

## driver = ready

`driver_step_types_from_file replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh` reports every type, but the honest set is `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"` — the rest are `not_implemented` stubs. The recipe needs exactly those four and nothing else.

Two things make this cell cheaper on hermes than on claudecode: (1) the approval is an ordinary `send`, not a modal keystroke, so no `keys` primitive is needed (contrast 2.19, which is `gap:keys` precisely because its modal never becomes a message row); (2) `wait_turn` covers BOTH turns — hermes' plan pause IS a completed turn, and the driver's `wait_turn` counts `finish_reason='stop'` rows monotonically against `EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN`, so the second call blocks for a NEW stop row rather than returning on the stale one. claudecode's recipe cannot `wait_turn` the plan turn at all (its plan turn ends on an open ExitPlanMode tool) and reaches the gate with a fixed sleep instead.

## Distinctness from 2.18 (why this is not a duplicate)

2.18 records the SAME `/plan` → pause entry but TERMINATES at the waiting gate (final state waiting). This cell continues PAST the pause: the waiting→working recovery, a real `write_file` creating `./mycli.py`, and the settle to ready. Stopping at waiting here would be a duplicate of 2.18 and is a FAILURE, not a pass.
caveats: RECORD-TIME RE-SPEC (settles the assessment's write_file assumption): this install exposes NO workspace file tool. The live roster, enumerated directly from model_tools.get_tool_definitions() under the recording HERMES_HOME, is 37 functions with no write_file/patch/read_file/search_files/terminal, and execute_code fails on "docker version". The gate is the recording home's config.yaml `terminal.backend: docker` (check_terminal_requirements/check_file_requirements return False), i.e. one config line rather than a hermes capability limit - flipping it to `local` restores write_file at the cost of giving the live agent host shell, which is a maintainer decision. The editor phase was therefore retargeted at skill_manage(action='create'), which writes a real SKILL.md under $HERMES_HOME/skills/. Nothing the cell asserts changes: irrlicht observes transitions, message rows and tool_calls, never file paths. What this cell does NOT prove is that hermes can edit a project source file - it cannot, in this configuration.

PROVISIONAL on emission (why confidence is 0.7, not higher). BOTH prose legs are model-behaviour bets on a generic heuristic, and they pull in opposite directions: the plan turn MUST end on a question/imperative cue or there is no waiting episode at all, and the implement turn MUST NOT end on one or it lands in waiting instead of ready and the turn_end phase fails. The recipe pins both sides in the prompt text (the plan skill's own Execution Handoff already prescribes '... Shall I proceed?'), but no recording has yet confirmed hermes emits the cue-bearing row for the plan turn or a cue-free row for the implement turn. That is a recipe/agent-behaviour outcome, not a parser defect: the daemon chain (parser.go -> messageFold -> classifyAgentDone -> transcript_activity) is verified by code read. record settles it.

The acceptance bullet 'within one turn: two model contributions recorded, each with its own ModelName' is NOT expressible on hermes and is deliberately not asserted. The adapter reads only the `sessions` row (one model) and never `session_model_usage`, where hermes actually attributes per-(model, task) usage including aux calls. Under instantiation (b) one model throughout is the EXPECTED shape (the claudecode sibling asserts the same single-ModelName property), so this is a scenario-reading note, not a daemon defect — hence a caveat and not `bug`. Do not read this cell as evidence irrlicht can see hermes' auxiliary-model spend: it cannot, and the data is sitting in a table the adapter does not query.

NO metric observations are pinned, and this is load-bearing rather than an oversight. `of verify` hard-asserts the observations block against the REPLAY GOLDEN summary (tools/onboarding-factory/internal/validate/observations.go, applyHardAssertions), and the replay path runs `hermes.Parser` over a transcript only (tools/onboarding-factory/cmd/replay/main.go registers `&hermes.Parser{}`) — never ComputeMetrics, which is where hermes' tokens and cost come from. A hermes golden therefore reports cum_input+cum_output = 0, so `tokens_nonzero` / `cost_nonzero` would FAIL, and `total_tokens_nonzero` is gated to antigravity at cmd/replay/metrics.go. The cross-phase token growth this scenario cares about is asserted on the LIVE metrics surface in the recipe's verify[] instead. Two sibling cells (2.1 basic-turn, 2.18) still pin tokens/cost and carry the same latent drift; it is latent only because hermes has no recordings yet (no golden -> ValidateObservations skips). Unlock: extend the #766 store-vector lift + StageReplayStore to hermes as #775/#776 did for antigravity.

Plan-skill obedience on the SECOND turn. The skill body ('For this turn, you are planning only. Do not implement code.') is expanded into the first user message and therefore stays in conversation history. A model that over-generalizes it could refuse to implement on the approval turn, which would end the run in waiting or in a no-tool ready. The approval step's text explicitly declares plan mode over and names the file to write; if a recording still shows the refusal, that is a prompt fix, not a pillar change.

cwd fragility (inherited from the column): `hermes chat` writes source='cli' rows and those carry no cwd, so both DiscoverPID and the project binding fall back to the live-process CWD, which returns nothing when more than one non-service hermes SESSION process is alive. The recording must not run a second interactive hermes session concurrently (a long-lived gateway is fine — isServiceArgv excludes it).

Rig prerequisite (inherited, not a driver step-type gap): there is still no HERMES_HOME wiring under tools/onboarding-factory/scripts, and hermes writes no transcript file — the driver reports transcript.path as the pseudo-path '<store>?session=<id>' and has no store->JSONL exporter like opencode's. run-cell.sh only checks the path is non-empty, but curation/replay need a real file, so record may have to port an exporter before a transcript.jsonl + golden exist for this column at all.

`model` is deliberately unpinned (#440): the recorded model is whatever model.default the run's HERMES_HOME config.yaml carries (live: gpt-5.6-luna on provider openai-codex, which irrlicht's capacity table prices). record fills observations.model from the recording. A recording home pointed at an unpriced local model (e.g. google/gemma-4-26b-a4b, also present in the live store) would price at 0 — a pricing-table gap, not a daemon defect.

OpenToolStalled risk (an EXTRA waiting, not a missing one): if the editor's skill_manage call lingered past the OpenToolStalled threshold, the classifier would emit an earlier 'stalled edit tool -> likely permission prompt -> waiting' inside a phase. The spec's phases are relative and not exhaustive, so the arc still verifies, and it cannot manufacture the FINAL ready - record should note the extra episode rather than treat it as a defect. It is a false-positive route on hermes specifically: skill_manage has no approval call, so no real permission prompt exists behind it.

sources.note: The architect/editor pair in hermes' own words. Frontmatter name=plan v2.0.0, tags include plan-mode; first heading '# Plan Mode'; Core behavior 'For this turn, you are planning only. Do not implement code.'; Save location '.hermes/plans/YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS-<slug>.md' via write_file; and '## Execution Handoff' (line 314): 'After saving the plan, offer the execution approach: \"Plan complete and saved. Ready to execute using subagent-driven-development — ... Shall I proceed?\"' followed by 'When executing, use the subagent-driven-development skill'. This is the whole instantiation-(b) shape: plan -> ask -> execute.

Negative scan anchoring the (a)-is-absent half of agent=partial: a full-tree case-insensitive grep for 'architect' over the installed 0.19.0 source (excluding node_modules and the architecture/architectural word-family) matches ONLY plugins/hermes-achievements/dashboard/plugin_api.py's 'Vibe Architect' achievement and two creative skill docs (popular-web-designs/templates/cohere.md, humanizer/SKILL.md). No --architect flag, no two-model turn loop. Version confirmed live: `hermes --version` -> 'Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) - upstream d0b87dad', install method git.

DEFAULT_CONFIG['auxiliary'] (the section that could have carried a second model): per-task slots for vision, web_extract, compression, skills_hub, approval, curator, kanban_decomposer, plus the post-turn goal-judge call ('After every turn, a lightweight judge call asks the auxiliary model'). Each slot defaults provider='auto', model='' (the provider's default aux model). These are SIDE tasks - none of them emits the turn's edits - which is why the auxiliary section does not make hermes an instantiation-(a) agent.

Two facts that decide the token half. (1) record_auxiliary_usage -> _record_model_usage writes a per-(model, provider, task) delta into session_model_usage 'WITHOUT touching the sessions summary row' (docstring, issue #23270) - so an aux model's contribution never reaches the aggregate the irrlicht adapter reads. (2) update_token_counts' non-absolute branch INCREMENTS (input_tokens = input_tokens + ?), and absolute=True is documented as the gateway path only - so for a `hermes chat` session the sessions aggregate is strictly non-decreasing across the plan and implement phases, which is the cross-phase accumulation this scenario asserts.

Live read-only evidence (sqlite3 file:...?mode=ro) that per-model attribution exists but is out of the adapter's reach. session_model_usage schema: PRIMARY KEY (session_id, model, billing_provider, billing_base_url, billing_mode, task). Session 20260726_190232_65c19a has three rows - main loop task='' (4 API calls, 17616 in / 188 out), 'approval' (1 call, 301/7), 'title_generation' (1 call, 89/38) - while its sessions row exposes ONE model. Across all cli/tui sessions, no session has >1 distinct model (aux provider 'auto' resolves back to the primary, gpt-5.6-luna).

The adapter's read surface, cited by symbol (the file is under active edit). querySessionMetrics selects model/cwd/end_reason/started_at/ended_at/input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_read_tokens/cache_write_tokens FROM sessions WHERE source IN ('cli','tui'); ModelName = firstNonEmpty(model,'unknown') and TotalTokens = input+output. session_model_usage is never queried. foldMessages replays the messages rows through Parser, and messageFold.apply carries the leg this cell depends on: on ev.EventType == 'user_message' it sets pendingWaitingCue = false ('A new user message answers whatever the agent was waiting on, so the cue does not survive it'), which is what makes waiting -> working possible on the approval reply.

The turn-boundary + cue chain, by symbol: ParseLine sets ev.PendingWaitingCue = session.ProseIndicatesWaiting(tailer.WaitingScanWindow(text)) from the FULL assistant text BEFORE TruncateAssistantText, and rewrites the same row to turn_done when finishReasonEndsTurn(finish_reason) - a denylist whose only continuing value is 'tool_calls'. Cue and turn boundary therefore arrive together, so the plan pause IS the turn boundary; and the implement turn's cue-free stop row settles to ready by the same rule.

The ladder that produces the arc. classifyAgentDone checks IsWaitingForUserInput() BEFORE routing turn_done to ready ('turn ended with question or cue -> waiting'), giving working -> waiting with no intervening ready. For the recovery leg, once the approval user row clears the cue and IsAgentDone() goes false, no higher rule claims the pass on a hermes session (no PermissionPending, no user-blocking tool, no hook-tier idle_prompt), so the total default rule transcript_activity fires: 'transcript activity (waiting -> working)'.

driver = ready, from the honest set: DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn" (every other step type is a not_implemented stub). The recipe needs exactly those four. SEAM 2's wait_turn polls COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop' and only returns when the count exceeds EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN, so the second wait_turn blocks for a NEW stop row rather than returning on the plan turn's.

Why the editor phase is ungated (no second waiting episode to design around): that cell established, from hermes source, that check_all_command_guards is imported by exactly ONE module, tools/terminal_tool.py, and that tools/file_tools.py write_file has no approval call at all. The implement phase's file write therefore cannot raise hermes' human approval modal - the modal that makes 2.19 itself daemon=incapable / driver=gap:keys.

The canonical instantiation-(b) sibling this recipe is templated from: plan phase -> approval -> editor phase, one model throughout, asserting the post-approval continuation + a real edit + cross-phase token accumulation, and explicitly NOT stopping at the waiting gate (which would duplicate 2.18). Its spec's 5 phases (session_birth, architect_plan, plan_gate, editor_implement, turn_end) are mirrored here with hermes' presession-aware anchoring.

Why no metric observations are pinned: the replay registry maps hermes to &hermes.Parser{} only - the golden is produced by replaying a transcript through the Parser, never by ComputeMetrics over the SQLite store, which is where hermes' tokens/cost/model actually come from. Combined with cmd/replay/metrics.go gating TotalTokens/ContextWindow/ContextUtilization to antigravity, a hermes golden would report zero tokens and fail any tokens_nonzero/cost_nonzero hard assertion.

preconditions: hermes >=0.19.0 on PATH (verified live: 'Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)', git install - the CLI is a Python console-script shim into <HERMES_HOME>/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes)
HERMES_HOME exported to the recording home, with config.yaml carrying model.default + model.provider and credentials in .env/auth.json, so the run writes to an isolated state.db

the bundled `plan` skill present in the recording home's skills dir - verify with scan_skill_commands() returning '/plan', or that <skills>/software-development/plan/SKILL.md exists. Without it `/plan` falls through to prefix-matching and the architect phase never happens
sqlite3 on PATH - hermes persists no transcript file, so the driver reads the session id and BOTH turn completions straight out of state.db (the driver hard-fails without it)
tmux on PATH: `/plan` is an in-REPL slash command, so the live-TUI path is required (there is no headless way to deliver it)
irrlichd is recording - run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a daemon started with --record

no second hermes SESSION process running concurrently - source='cli' rows carry no stored cwd and the live-process CWD fallback returns nothing when more than one session process is alive (a running gateway is fine)
setup: The driver launches `hermes chat` under tmux in a fresh per-run cwd and polls the pane for 'Type your message or /help' before typing - the TUI loads tools and skills for several seconds and swallows keystrokes sent before it is ready.

RE-SPEC AT RECORD TIME - what the editor phase edits, and why. The assessment's recipe had the editor phase write ./mycli.py with `write_file`. That tool DOES NOT EXIST in this install: the live roster (enumerated directly from model_tools.get_tool_definitions() under the recording HERMES_HOME - 37 callable functions) has no write_file, patch, read_file, search_files, terminal or web_search, and `execute_code` fails with "Docker command is available but 'docker version' failed". The cause is one config line, not a hermes limitation: the recording home's config.yaml sets `terminal:\n  backend: docker`, and check_terminal_requirements()/check_file_requirements() gate the whole terminal+file toolset behind a working backend. Flipping it to `local` would restore write_file - but it also grants the live agent host shell access, which is a maintainer's call and not one a recording subagent should make silently, so the recipe was retargeted at the callable roster instead (the same move commit 010a6fc1 made for the 2.4 sibling: 'drive hermes/self-correction-iteration with skill_view, not the file tools').

The editor's artifact is therefore a SKILL FILE, not a workspace source file: `skill_manage(action='create', ...)` writes a real SKILL.md under $HERMES_HOME/skills/<category>/<name>/ (verified by calling the handler directly before recording: {"success": true, "skill_md": "<HERMES_HOME>/skills/software-development/<name>/SKILL.md"}). This substitution is INVISIBLE at the layer this cell asserts - irrlicht observes state transitions, message rows and tool_calls, never file paths - so every acceptance criterion (topology, visible waiting, final ready, tool calls >= 1, one ModelName, cross-phase token growth) is met by the same evidence it would have been met by with write_file. What is genuinely lost is only the claim 'hermes edited a project source file', and the caveats record that.

ARCHITECT (plan phase): `/plan <task>` is intercepted by cli.py as a skill slash command - it expands the skill body plus the instruction into a single message on _pending_input, so it lands in state.db as one ordinary `user` row and drives a normal turn. The plan is deliberately WIDE (seven named sections, six+ numbered steps): the watcher polls every 2s with a 500ms debounce, so a short turn can commit its user row and its stop row inside a SINGLE scan and the ready->working edge never exists to be observed.

The plan prompt pins the exact closing line ('Shall I proceed with implementing this plan?'). This is load-bearing: hermes has no structured approval gate, so the ONLY thing that makes the pause observable is a trailing question/imperative cue in the turn's final assistant text (ProseIndicatesWaiting). Proven live by the 2.18 sibling recording, whose stop row ends on exactly that sentence and drove 'turn ended with question or cue -> waiting'.

The first `wait_turn` is legitimate even though the turn ends in `waiting` (unlike the claudecode sibling, whose plan turn ends on an OPEN ExitPlanMode tool and had to reach the gate with a fixed sleep). Hermes' plan pause IS a completed turn: the driver polls for a new role='assistant' finish_reason='stop' row, which the pause writes.

The 8s sleep after the plan turn holds the waiting episode open long enough for the watcher to have published working->waiting before the approval reply arrives - otherwise the two transitions can coalesce into one poll tick and the waiting phase goes missing.

EDITOR (implement phase): the approval is an ordinary `send`, not a modal keystroke - hermes' plan gate is prose, so no `keys` primitive is needed. The text does four jobs: (1) it answers the question, which is what resets pendingWaitingCue in messageFold.apply and drives waiting->working; (2) it declares plan mode over, because the skill body ('for this turn you are planning only') is still in conversation history and a literal-minded model would otherwise refuse to implement; (3) it pre-authorizes the creation, because skill_manage's own description tells the model to 'Confirm with user before creating/deleting' and a confirmation question would land the turn in waiting instead of ready; (4) it forbids ending the reply with a question, for the same reason.

No settings blob is needed and none is passed. skill_manage has no approval call (hermes' only human approval gate is check_all_command_guards, imported in production code solely by tools/terminal_tool.py), so the implement phase is ungated by construction - the hermes equivalent of the claudecode recipe's permissions.allow[Edit,Write], for free.

The trailing 16s sleep lets the implement turn's working->ready settle land and be published before the driver tears the tmux session down. The claudecode sibling lost a whole recording to exactly this race.

HOUSEKEEPING: the created skill is removed from the recording home after promotion, so the next cell in the sweep starts from the same 68-skill roster this one did (a leftover skill adds a slash command and grows every later system prompt).

script.text: /plan Create a new Hermes skill named mycli-version-flag, in category software-development, that documents how to add a --version flag to a small single-file Python CLI so it prints 0.1.0 and exits. IMPORTANT: this session has NO workspace file tools (write_file, patch, read_file and terminal are not in your tool roster) - the ONLY tool that can create the skill is skill_manage. Write the plan directly in your reply as markdown, with the sections Goal, Assumptions, Step-by-step plan (at least six numbered steps), The exact skill_manage call you will make, Validation, and Risks. Do not create anything yet and do not call any tool this turn. End your reply with exactly this line: Shall I proceed with implementing this plan?

Approved - proceed now. Plan mode is over for this turn: implement the plan yourself, right here, without delegating. Call skill_manage with action='create', name='mycli-version-flag', category='software-development' and a SKILL.md body that follows the plan you just wrote. You already have my approval, so do not ask for confirmation. When the tool returns, end your reply with a plain one-sentence statement of what you created - do not ask me anything and do not end with a question.

verify: events.jsonl shows the hermes session (id shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_xxxxxx) born ready; a transient proc-<PID> presession may also appear and is NOT the session the arc lands on
events.jsonl shows ready -> working when the /plan turn starts (architect/plan phase)
events.jsonl shows working -> waiting when the plan turn completes - and NO state_transition to ready between those two
events.jsonl shows waiting -> working on the SAME session after the approval message is sent (editor/implement phase; this is the leg 2.18 does not have)

events.jsonl shows working -> ready on the SAME session when the implement turn finishes - final state is ready, NOT waiting. A recording that ends in waiting is a duplicate of 2.18 and is a FAILURE of this cell, not a pass
